memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Israelites sampled their provisions but did not inquire of the Lord. Then Joshua made a treaty of peace with them to let them live, and the leaders of the assembly ratified it by oath. — Josh 9:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the heart of the whole chapter, captured in one devastating phrase: "but did not inquire of the Lord." The Israelites examined the evidence with their own eyes — they "sampled their provisions," inspecting the mouldy bread and worn gear. They relied on their own senses and judgment. And they made their decision without once asking God. That single omission led them into a treaty they would come to regret.

This is one of the most instructive failures in all of Scripture, precisely because it is so relatable. Israel did not commit some dramatic, obvious sin. They simply made an important decision based on appearances, trusting their own assessment, and forgot to pray. They leaned on what they could see rather than seeking the God who sees everything.

How easily we do the same. We face a decision, we weigh the visible evidence, we consult our own reasoning, and we act — all without truly bringing the matter to God. The evidence in front of us seems clear enough, so we never think to ask. Yet the Gibeonites' mouldy bread teaches us that appearances can deceive, and our own judgment, however sensible, is limited.

The remedy is beautifully simple: inquire of the Lord. Before the big decisions and even the small ones, we are invited to seek God's guidance. "Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding; in all your ways submit to him, and he will make your paths straight" (Prov 3:5-6). Israel leaned on their own understanding and stumbled. Let us learn from them to seek God first, in everything.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you tend to make decisions based on appearances without inquiring of the Lord?
2. What decision are you facing right now that you have not truly brought to God?
3. How can you build the habit of seeking God's guidance before you act?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for the times I lean on my own understanding and forget to seek You. Teach me to inquire of You in all my decisions, trusting You to guide my path. Amen.
